name: Shoulder Press Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with an upright back pad and handles level with your ears that travel straight up overhead.
instructions: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back flat against the pad.
Take both handles, palms facing forward.
Press straight up until your arms are almost locked.
Lower under control back to ear level.
keyCues: Keep your ribs down and your core braced.
Stop just short of locking the elbows.
Press up, not forward.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back away from the pad.
Setting the seat so low the range gets uncomfortably deep.
Letting the handles crash back down.

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
machineIdentification: An adjustable bench set upright, plus a pair of dumbbells.
instructions: Set a bench back to just short of vertical.
Sit with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
Kick them up to shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Press overhead until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower back to ear level under control.
keyCues: Keep your lower back in contact with the pad.
Don't clash the dumbbells at the top.
Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.
commonMistakes: Arching the back to press heavier weights.
Only lowering halfway.
Letting the elbows drift far forward at the bottom.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
machineIdentification: A barbell in a rack set at roughly upper-chest height. You press it standing, so nothing supports your torso.
instructions: Set the bar at upper-chest height and grip just outside your shoulders.
Unrack and step back, bar resting on your front shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Press the bar overhead, moving your head back out of the way.
Lower under control to your collarbone.
keyCues: Finish with the bar over the middle of your feet.
Squeeze your glutes to stop the back arching.
Push your head through once the bar clears it.
commonMistakes: Leaning back into a standing incline press.
Pressing around the face instead of moving the head.
Losing core brace between reps.

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
machineIdentification: A barbell fixed inside vertical rails so it can only travel straight up and down. Twist the bar to lock it at any height.
instructions: Set an upright bench under the bar.
Sit so the bar lines up just in front of your face.
Unlock the bar with a small twist of the wrists.
Press up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower to chin height under control.
keyCues: Position the bench so the bar path clears your nose.
Keep your back flat against the pad.
Re-lock the bar before letting go.
commonMistakes: Sitting too far back so the bar scrapes your face.
Bouncing the bar off the bottom of the range.
Forgetting to lock the bar at the end of the set.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lower slowly back to your sides.
keyCues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Stop at shoulder height — no higher.
Go lighter than feels right; this one rewards control.
commonMistakes: Swinging the weights up with a hip thrust.
Shrugging so the traps take over from the shoulders.
Raising past shoulder height and losing tension.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
machineIdentification: A single cable pulley set at the lowest position with a D-handle. You stand side-on to the tower.
instructions: Set a pulley at the bottom with a D-handle.
Stand side-on and take the handle in your outside hand.
Let your arm hang across your body.
Raise your arm out to shoulder height.
Lower slowly, then switch sides.
keyCues: Keep tension on the cable even at the bottom.
Lead with the elbow.
Stand tall — don't lean away from the tower.
commonMistakes: Leaning hard away to use body weight as a counterbalance.
Letting the arm swing rather than lift.
Going too heavy and recruiting the traps.

name: Rear Delt Fly Machine
machineIdentification: Usually the pec deck run in reverse — you sit facing the chest pad and pull the arms backward instead of together. Some gyms have a dedicated station.
instructions: Set the handles so they start in front of you at shoulder height.
Sit facing the pad with your chest against it.
Take a handle in each hand, elbows slightly bent.
Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc.
Return slowly to the front.
keyCues: Think about pulling your elbows apart.
Keep your chest on the pad throughout.
Pause for a beat at the back.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows and rowing instead of flying.
Using momentum from the torso.
Shrugging the shoulders up as the arms travel back.

name: Face Pull
machineIdentification: A cable pulley set at roughly face height with a rope attachment. You stand facing it and pull the rope toward your eyes.
instructions: Set a pulley just above head height and attach a rope.
Grip both rope ends with thumbs pointing back.
Step back until the cable is taut, arms extended.
Pull the rope toward your forehead, spreading your hands apart.
Return slowly to full extension.
keyCues: Keep your elbows high, level with your shoulders.
Pull the rope apart as much as back.
Stay light — this is a health move, not a strength one.
commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows so it becomes a row.
Leaning back to counterbalance heavy weight.
Rushing reps without pausing at the finish.
